# Team Onboarding Checklist

**Version:** 1.0  
**Last Updated:** 2026-02-08  
**Purpose:** Ensure consistent, comprehensive onboarding for new team members joining OctoAcme projects

## Purpose
This comprehensive onboarding checklist helps new team members get up to speed quickly while ensuring they understand processes, tools, and their role in the project. Use this for all new team members, regardless of role.

---

## Day 1: Welcome and Setup

### Administrative
- [ ] Complete HR paperwork and system access requests
- [ ] Receive company laptop and necessary hardware
- [ ] Set up email, calendar, and Slack/Teams accounts
- [ ] Add to relevant distribution lists and team channels
- [ ] Review company policies and code of conduct

### Team Introductions
- [ ] Meet with direct manager for orientation
- [ ] Introduction to team members (scheduled 1:1s)
- [ ] Added to team org chart
- [ ] Assigned an onboarding buddy/mentor

### Initial Access
- [ ] GitHub organization and repository access
- [ ] Project management tool access (e.g., GitHub Projects, Jira)
- [ ] Documentation repository access
- [ ] CI/CD pipeline access (read-only initially)

---

## Week 1: Process and Context

### Project Documentation Review
- [ ] Review [OctoAcme Project Management Overview](../octoacme-project-management-overview.md)
- [ ] Read [Roles and Personas](../octoacme-roles-and-personas.md) documentation
- [ ] Review current project charter and one-pager
- [ ] Understand project goals, success metrics, and timeline
- [ ] Review risk register and known dependencies

### Process Understanding
- [ ] Review [Project Initiation Guide](../octoacme-project-initiation.md)
- [ ] Review [Project Planning](../octoacme-project-planning.md) process
- [ ] Review [Execution & Tracking](../octoacme-execution-and-tracking.md) workflow
- [ ] Understand [Release & Deployment](../octoacme-release-and-deployment.md) process
- [ ] Review [Risk Management & Communication](../octoacme-risks-and-communication.md) protocols

### Team Rhythm
- [ ] Attend first daily standup
- [ ] Understand meeting cadence (standups, sprint planning, retros)
- [ ] Added to all recurring team meetings
- [ ] Review past sprint retrospective notes
- [ ] Understand escalation paths and communication norms

---

## Week 2: Technical Setup and Role-Specific Training

### Development Environment (for technical roles)
- [ ] Clone project repositories
- [ ] Set up local development environment
- [ ] Run project locally and verify functionality
- [ ] Review coding standards and style guides
- [ ] Understand branching strategy and PR workflow
- [ ] Complete first code review (shadow mode)

### Role-Specific Orientation

#### For Developers
- [ ] Review architecture documentation
- [ ] Set up debugging tools and IDE configurations
- [ ] Run test suite locally and understand test strategy
- [ ] Review CI/CD pipelines and deployment process
- [ ] Shadow a code review session
- [ ] Assigned first small task or bug fix

#### For Product Managers
- [ ] Review product roadmap and vision documents
- [ ] Understand customer personas and market positioning
- [ ] Review analytics dashboards and key metrics
- [ ] Shadow customer research or user interview session
- [ ] Review competitive analysis and market trends

#### For Project Managers
- [ ] Review current project plan and milestones
- [ ] Understand resource allocation and team capacity
- [ ] Review risk register and mitigation strategies
- [ ] Shadow weekly status update meeting
- [ ] Review stakeholder communication templates

#### For UX/UI Designers
- [ ] Review design system and component library
- [ ] Access design tools (Figma, Sketch, etc.)
- [ ] Review past user research findings
- [ ] Understand accessibility standards and guidelines
- [ ] Shadow a design review session

#### For Technical Writers
- [ ] Review existing documentation structure
- [ ] Access documentation tools and publishing systems
- [ ] Review style guide and documentation standards
- [ ] Understand documentation release process
- [ ] Shadow a documentation review

#### For Security Leads
- [ ] Review security policies and compliance requirements
- [ ] Access security scanning tools and dashboards
- [ ] Review past threat models and security assessments
- [ ] Understand incident response procedures
- [ ] Review security training materials

#### For Support Engineers
- [ ] Access support ticketing system
- [ ] Review support playbooks and troubleshooting guides
- [ ] Shadow experienced support engineer
- [ ] Review common issues and resolution patterns
- [ ] Understand escalation procedures

#### For Business Analysts
- [ ] Review business requirements documents
- [ ] Understand data analysis tools and reports
- [ ] Review process flow diagrams
- [ ] Shadow requirements gathering session
- [ ] Understand validation and acceptance procedures

#### For QA/Testing
- [ ] Review test plans and test cases
- [ ] Access testing environments and tools
- [ ] Understand test automation framework
- [ ] Review defect tracking and triage process
- [ ] Shadow a testing cycle

---

## Week 3-4: Contribution and Integration

### Active Participation
- [ ] Participate actively in sprint planning
- [ ] Complete first meaningful task/deliverable
- [ ] Provide input in team retrospective
- [ ] Begin regular contributions to project board
- [ ] Start taking on regular role responsibilities

### Relationship Building
- [ ] Schedule 1:1s with key cross-functional partners
- [ ] Attend cross-team meetings relevant to role
- [ ] Join relevant communities of practice
- [ ] Understand how to request help and provide feedback

### Feedback and Adjustment
- [ ] 30-day check-in with manager
- [ ] Provide feedback on onboarding process
- [ ] Identify knowledge gaps or additional training needs
- [ ] Set goals for next 30-60 days

---

## 60-Day Milestone

- [ ] Fully integrated into team workflow
- [ ] Independently managing assigned responsibilities
- [ ] Contributing to planning and decision-making
- [ ] Building relationships across teams
- [ ] Ready to onboard next new team member
